$comment: SEED CONSTANTS — advisory, not authoritative, and deliberately not wired
into the runtime by C7.
The spec (§Calibration harness & methodology) names spring constants, corner
smoothing values, tint thresholds, hysteresis rates, merge-distance defaults
and clear-variant dimming as DELEGATED UNKNOWNS: named in the design,
answered by the harness, recorded into calibration profiles. This file is
that record as of C7's landing.
Every entry carries its own provenance and status. That matters more than the
numbers, because the two statuses mean very different things:
measured    — derived from a real measurement, with the run that produced
it named. Usable as a seed today.
unmeasured  — the harness cannot answer this yet, and the reason is stated.
A consumer must treat these as absent, NOT as zero and not as
the advisory default's endorsement.
Nothing here is a threshold. Thresholds are per tier and per engine cell,
decided against holdout fixtures, and they belong to C9.
$colorSpaceNote: X5 locks v1 calibration to sRGB. A number here measured in another space would not be comparable to anything else in the pipeline.

$comment: The corner reference. These come from S2, which recomputed Apple's
`.continuous` corner from a macOS 26 CGPath dump and asserted the geometry
from the control points alone — a stronger provenance than anything C7's
own captures could give, since a rasterised corner cannot recover the
curve that drew it to this precision.
X8 makes the two-reference model binding: `apple-continuous` is the
Apple-direct fit that `profile: "continuous"` resolves to, and
`figma-smoothing` is the separate interpolable authoring axis. Morphs
across the two throw. The smoothing number below is the documented route
ONTO the interpolable axis, not a redefinition of the Apple reference.

edgeReachPerRadius.note: Not reverse-engineered: Apple publishes it as +[CALayer cornerCurveExpansionFactor:] for kCACornerCurveContinuous.

appleContinuousCorner.structure: three cubics per corner, no arc primitive — but the middle cubic IS a genuine circular arc

midArc.note: The handle identity (4/3)·tan(sweep/4)·R matching to 1.5e-7 is the real proof the middle cubic is an arc; radius and centre alone could be a coincidence of symmetry.

continuity.atStraightEdgeJoin: G2 — zero curvature. This is the join that reads visually, and Apple gets it right.

atShoulderArcJoins.note: Apple's own path is not even G1 here. Every 'smooth corner' article assuming G2 throughout is describing a curve Apple does not draw. This is the single most useful number for calibration: it is the reference's OWN normal discontinuity, so a specular-rim residual at these joins is a property of the target, not a defect in vitrea, and chasing gradient precision below it is chasing an artifact.

radiusSaturation.note: Apple warps the corner past this ratio, under a different budget policy from Figma's. Shapes above it are NOT comparable to Apple and must be excluded from fidelity claims or measured separately.

note: The widely cited 'Figma smoothing 0.6 = iOS' is NOT the best fit — 0.6 is
nearly 2x worse (3.613e-3 r). This answers the spec's 'corner smoothing
It is informational rather than load-bearing, and the reason is the
important part: routing the field fit through Figma's family costs 6.4x
the value error of fitting the same field directly to Apple's curve
(0.670px vs 0.104px), because the reference gap (1.96e-3 r) exceeds the
field's own deviation against Apple (1.38e-3 r). S2's verdict was that
the reference family, not the field, was the fidelity bottleneck — so v1
fits Apple directly and this number exists only for authors who want a

fieldResidualAgainstApple.provenance: docs/doperpowers/spikes/2026-08-24-s2-geometry-field-findings.md §3, family D (rsupn) fit to Apple directly
fieldResidualAgainstApple.note: Recorded so C7's own shape metrics have a floor to compare against: a measured contour distance at or below this is at the field's approximation limit, not a tuning opportunity. Note the gradient max (1.752°) sits BELOW the reference's own 2.4532° tangent break.

$comment: This is where C7's capture wall bites. Every parameter below needs pixels
of the composited material, and on this machine there are none — Liquid
Glass is composited by the window server and ScreenCaptureKit is TCC-denied
(apps/reference-apple/README.md §'The capture wall'). The provisional
fixtures are pixel-identical to their backgrounds, so fitting anything to
them would be fitting to the background.
Each entry therefore records the METHOD that will answer it and the fixture
scenes that method needs, so the measurement is a re-run rather than a
redesign once the grant lands. The advisory defaults already in the runtime
stand until then — that is the spec's stated fallback ('advisory defaults
hold until fixtures land').

blurSigma.method: blurEdgeSpread over the impulse and checkerboard scenes — the spec mandates both precisely because a material's response to an impulse IS its kernel, and a checkerboard supplies many step edges per capture.
blurSigma.note: Expected to be size-parameterised, not one constant: the spec's acceptance #2 asserts a larger surface shows stronger lensing and deeper shadow over the same backdrop, so the fit must be per component size across rrect-sm/md/lg before any single number is recorded.

luminanceTransfer.method: luminanceTransfer slope/offset against the light-solid, dark-solid and photo backgrounds, in linear light.

tintResponse.method: tintResponse in OKLab against the photo background, which is the only canonical background carrying saturated hue transitions.

rimIntensity.method: rimIntensity peak and radial profile width near the contour.
rimIntensity.note: Read this one against geometry.appleContinuousCorner.continuity.atShoulderArcJoins: a rim discontinuity at the shoulder joins is expected, because the reference curve has a 2.4532° tangent break there.

shadowFalloff.method: shadowFalloff peak and decay length outside the contour, across the size sweep.

samplingPadding.provenance: Decision Log #19 — an advisory default explicitly marked calibration-delegated.
samplingPadding.note: S1 makes the real constraint structural rather than tunable: samplingPadding must be >= 3σ of the group's blur radius, so this number is downstream of blurSigma and cannot be answered before it. 24px is 3σ at σ=8.

mergeDistance.method: The toolbar-group scene at spacing 12 shows whether the two implementations union proximity alike; the union aesthetics the spec caps (neck width, max bulge, separation threshold) are read off the same capture.
mergeDistance.note: Constrained by S1 to be >= samplingPadding, so it is downstream of blurSigma too.

clearVariantDimming.note: Doubly blocked, and the second reason is C7's own: the canonical matrix captures the regular variant only. Calibrating clear needs clear-variant scenes added to scenes.json, which is a scope question for C9 rather than a re-run of this harness.

$comment: Spring constants and hysteresis rates are named delegated unknowns, and
they are C9's by the spec's own division: motion metrics need frame
sequences, and full motion capture is out of C7's scope. The pressed scenes
in the canonical matrix capture the SETTLED pressed pose, not a transient,
so they constrain peak compression only — and not even that until the
material renders.

springConstants.method: Frame-sequence capture; packages/calibration exposes the motion metric family as types with morphSilhouetteTrajectory implemented.

adaptationHysteresis.provenance: Decision Log #19 — advisory 15Hz readback ceiling, calibration-delegated.
